summary:
Reviewed /Users/atharv/buisnessfind/data/store.js (293 lines) and /Users/atharv/buisnessfind/server.js (520 lines). The bones are better than most first drafts: scrypt with a real salt and timingSafeEqual, session tokens stored only as sha256 digests, an opaque HttpOnly cookie, mutual-accept friendship with no stranger discovery, correct share directionality in friendLocations(), and no IDOR in respondToRequest/unsavePlace. That is a genuinely decent starting point.

But the app as designed is not safe to make public, for three reasons that compound. (1) IDENTITY IS UNVERIFIED AND ENUMERABLE. There is no email verification anywhere, and friend discovery is by email address. Anyone can register victim@gmail.com; when the victim's real friend types that address into "add friend", they hand their live location to the impostor. Two working account-enumeration oracles exist — signup returns 409 "An account with that email already exists", and POST /api/friends/request returns 404 "No account with that email" (authenticated, but accounts are free and unverified, and the endpoint allows 60 checks/minute = ~86k email probes/day). There is a third, subtler oracle: login runs scryptSync only when the email exists, so a known email answers in ~80ms and an unknown one in ~0ms — a clean timing oracle regardless of the generic error string.

(2) LOCATION FUZZING IS NOT A PRIVACY CONTROL. Rounding to 2dp is a deterministic snap to a fixed ~1.11km x ~0.98km lattice. It is stable across observations, so it never averages away, and it leaks two ways: a friend polling /api/friends/locations builds a time series of grid cells, and the cell occupied nightly is the home cell; and when GPS jitter straddles a cell boundary, the observed value flips between two adjacent cells, localising the user to that boundary line at far better than 1km. The home-cell/work-cell pair is close to unique per person even at kilometre granularity (the Golle-Partridge result). And crucially the threat model here is not a stranger — it is the friend, who already knows your neighbourhood, so conditional on their prior the cell is often decisive. Worse, db.locations entries never expire: share once, forget, and your last known position (frequently your home, at 3am) stays visible to that friend forever. There is also no way to see who can currently see you, no access log, no share expiry, and nothing stops /api/location from being written when nobody is sharing.

(3) BLOCKING DOES NOT EXIST AND HARASSMENT IS UNBOUNDED. pendingRequestBetween() only looks at status 'pending', so a declined request can be re-sent immediately and forever. There is no cap on outgoing requests, no block model, no report model.

Beyond those, concrete defects: scryptSync blocks the single event loop (~80ms per login/signup, and /api/auth/* is exempt from the IP rate limiter entirely, so unauthenticated signup floods are a CPU DoS); loginAttempts is never pruned (unbounded memory) and its IP+email key lets anyone lock a known victim's email out for 15 minutes at will; the CSRF content-type check uses .includes('application/json'), which a CORS-safelisted `text/plain; x=application/json` passes, and it is absent from /api/auth/logout and from all of /api/friends, /api/location and /api/saved; save() rewrites the entire DB with a non-atomic writeFile, so a crash mid-write truncates the whole user database; /api/place and /api/nearby are unauthenticated, so one anonymous IP at the 30/min limit drains PLACE_DETAILS_DAILY_CAP=200 in seven minutes, denying the product's core feature to everyone and spending the owner's money doing it; savePlace stores unvalidated, uncapped name/category strings (stored-XSS payload if the frontend uses innerHTML, plus unbounded storage growth); publicUser leaks the email address of anyone who sends you a friend request; and precise user coordinates travel in GET query strings, so they land in every access and proxy log.

The specification below fixes all of it. Its central recommendation is a design change, not just a patch: make CHECK-INS the default social primitive ("I'm at Blue Tokai") and treat continuous live location as an explicit, time-boxed, always-expiring opt-in in the WhatsApp mould (15 min / 1 hr / 8 hrs, never "until I turn it off"). This satisfies the owner's copy — "see where your friends are headed" — with a fraction of the risk, keeps live coordinates in memory and off disk entirely, and makes the honest privacy-policy line "we do not store location history" literally true.

components.name: Password hashing and credential handling
components.purpose: Make login and signup cryptographically sound, non-enumerable, and incapable of stalling the single-threaded server.
components.design:
REPLACE scryptSync WITH ASYNC scrypt. crypto.scryptSync at N=16384,r=8,p=1,keylen=64 costs roughly 60-100ms and runs on the main thread. Node is single-threaded: every login blocks map searches, friend polls and static file serving for the full duration. Eight concurrent logins is ~0.7s of dead server. Use crypto.scrypt (callback -> promisified), which runs on the libuv threadpool. IMPORTANT SECOND STEP: the threadpool is also used by fs and DNS, and defaults to 4 threads, so unbounded async scrypt starves file reads and outbound fetch DNS. Set UV_THREADPOOL_SIZE=8 and put a semaphore in front of hashing that allows at most 3 concurrent derivations, queues the rest with a bounded queue (say 32), and returns 503 'Try again in a moment' when the queue is full. That bounds CPU spend per unit time regardless of attacker volume.

PARAMETERS. Move to N=2^15 (32768), r=8, p=1, keylen=32, and pass maxmem explicitly (64*1024*1024) because 128*N*r = 32MB exceeds Node's 32MB default and scrypt will throw. That lands near 150-200ms per hash; with concurrency 3 the ceiling is ~15 logins/sec, which is far more than this app needs. Store the params in the encoded string as it already does, but on verify CLAMP them to a whitelist ({N: [16384, 32768], r: 8, p: 1}) before passing to scrypt — currently verifyPassword feeds attacker-controllable N straight into scryptSync, so anyone who can write store.json can turn a login into an OOM. Add rehash-on-login: after a successful verify, if the stored params are below current policy, re-derive and persist silently.

ADD A PEPPER. New env var AUTH_PEPPER (32 random bytes, base64). Hash as scrypt(HMAC-SHA256(password, PEPPER), salt, ...). The pepper lives in .env, the hashes live in data/store.json, and .gitignore already separates them — so a leaked store.json alone becomes uncrackable. Encode a pepperVersion in the hash string so rotation is possible via rehash-on-login.

KILL THE LOGIN TIMING ORACLE. Today: `const user = store.findByEmail(...); const ok = user && store.verifyPassword(...)`. Unknown email short-circuits and answers instantly; known email spends 80ms. Fix: always run a verification. Keep a module-level DUMMY_HASH generated once at boot from a random password, and when the user is not found, verify the submitted password against DUMMY_HASH and discard the result. Same code path, same cost, same generic 401 'Email or password is incorrect.'

THROTTLING — three defects in the current design. (a) loginAttempts is a Map that is never pruned; ipHits has a sweeper, loginAttempts does not. Unbounded growth from a stream of distinct emails is a memory DoS. Add the same 60s sweeper, evicting entries older than ATTEMPT_WINDOW_MS. (b) attemptKey is `${remoteAddress}:${email}`, which means anyone can lock a known victim's email out of their own account for 15 minutes with 8 wrong guesses, repeatable forever — a griefing vector that scales. Replace the hard lock with progressive delay: attempts 1-3 free, then sleep 2^(n-3) * 250ms capped at 4s before answering, and only hard-429 after 20 failures in the window. Delay costs the attacker and barely inconveniences a fat-fingered user. (c) Add a SECOND, independent counter keyed on email alone (global across IPs) that trips at 50 failures/hour into a 'require email-link re-auth' state, because IPv6 /64 rotation makes per-IP counting alone worthless. (d) remoteAddress is the proxy IP behind any reverse proxy, collapsing every user into one bucket. Add TRUST_PROXY=1 env gating X-Forwarded-For parsing (rightmost-untrusted hop), and NEVER read that header when the flag is off — an unconditional read is a free rate-limit bypass.

PASSWORD POLICY. Min 10 chars (up from 8), max 128 (reject longer rather than truncate), reject if it equals or contains the local-part of the email or the display name case-insensitively, and reject against a bundled newline-delimited list of the top ~2000 breached passwords loaded once at boot (a ~20KB text file, zero dependencies). No composition rules — they push users toward Password1!.

MISSING FLOWS TO ADD. POST /api/auth/password/change (requires current password; rotates all sessions except the calling one; hard-stops all active location shares as a safety measure, because a password change often follows 'my ex had my phone'). POST /api/auth/password/forgot + /reset via single-use 30-minute tokens stored as sha256 digests in an emailTokens table, with /forgot always answering 202 regardless of whether the email exists.

components.name: Session and cookie layer
components.purpose: Give sessions visibility, revocability and sane lifetimes, and harden the cookie for a public deployment.
components.design:
WHAT IS ALREADY RIGHT. 32 random bytes as the token, sha256 digest stored server-side, raw token only in an HttpOnly cookie. This is correct and needs no HMAC or pepper — the token has full 256-bit entropy, so a plain digest is not brute-forceable. The Map lookup on the digest is not a meaningful timing side channel. Keep it.

COOKIE FLAGS. Current: Path=/, HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Max-Age, and Secure only when COOKIE_SECURE=1. Change Secure to DEFAULT ON with an explicit opt-out (COOKIE_INSECURE=1 for localhost dev). Default-off means a deploy that forgets one env var ships session tokens in cleartext, and SameSite=Lax does not prevent that. When Secure is on, rename the cookie to __Host-bf_session and drop the Domain attribute — the __Host- prefix makes it impossible for a sibling subdomain or a network attacker to overwrite the cookie, which is a real session-fixation defence. Add Priority=High. Send Cache-Control: no-store on every response that sets a cookie and on every /api response.

LIFETIME. 30 days absolute with no idle timeout is too generous for an app that discloses your position. Use a dual clock: idleExpires = 14 days from lastSeenAt (refreshed on use, at most once per hour to avoid a disk write per request), absoluteExpires = 90 days from creation, hard. userForToken must check both.

SESSION RECORDS AND DEVICE MANAGEMENT. Store per session: { userId, createdAt, lastSeenAt, idleExpires, absoluteExpires, uaHash (sha256 of User-Agent, truncated — never store the raw UA), ipPrefixHash (sha256 of the /24 or /48, so 'signed in from a new network' is detectable without storing IPs), label (derived, e.g. 'Chrome on Android') }. Expose GET /api/auth/sessions (list, current one flagged) and DELETE /api/auth/sessions/:id, plus POST /api/auth/logout-all. For a location-sharing app, being unable to see and kill an unknown device is a safety failure, not a convenience gap — a stalker's persistent session on a borrowed phone is exactly the scenario. Surface this in the UI as 'Signed-in devices' next to the sharing controls, not buried.

ROTATION. Regenerate the session token (new digest, delete old) on: successful login, password change, password reset, and email verification. Never reuse a pre-authentication token.

PRUNING. pruneSessions() runs once at boot only. Run it on an unref'd 15-minute interval as well, and cap sessions per user at 20 (evict least-recently-seen) so nobody can inflate store.json by looping login.

SECURITY HEADERS on every response (currently there are none): Content-Security-Policy with default-src 'self', script-src 'self' https://maps.googleapis.com, img-src 'self' data: https://*.googleapis.com https://*.gstatic.com https://*.ggpht.com, connect-src 'self' https://maps.googleapis.com, frame-ancestors 'none', base-uri 'none', object-src 'none'; X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff; Referrer-Policy: no-referrer; Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains when Secure is on; Permissions-Policy: geolocation=(self), interest-cohort=(). frame-ancestors 'none' also removes clickjacking as a way to trick someone into toggling a location share.

components.name: CSRF and request-integrity middleware
components.purpose: Make every state-changing endpoint uniformly unforgeable, rather than protecting only /api/auth by accident.
components.design:
THREE CONCRETE HOLES TODAY. (1) The content-type check uses `String(req.headers['content-type']).includes('application/json')`. The CORS simple-request safelist compares only the MIME essence and ignores parameters, so an attacker can send Content-Type: `text/plain; x=application/json` with no preflight, and that string passes .includes(). Parse properly: take the substring before the first ';', trim, lowercase, and require exact equality with 'application/json'. (2) The check sits AFTER the logout branch, so POST /api/auth/logout has no check at all. (3) /api/friends/*, /api/location and /api/saved perform no check whatsoever. Right now only SameSite=Lax stands between a malicious page and 'enable location sharing with attacker-controlled friend id' — a single browser-behaviour defence with no depth behind it.

SPECIFY ONE MIDDLEWARE, APPLIED TO EVERY NON-GET /api ROUTE, in this order:
(a) Method gate: GET/HEAD must be side-effect-free. Note that DELETE /api/saved?id= is currently the only mutation that carries no body — it must go through the same checks, so it needs the header token even though it has no content-type.
(b) Origin / Sec-Fetch-Site: if Sec-Fetch-Site is present, require 'same-origin' (or 'none' for direct navigation, which cannot be a mutation anyway). Else if Origin is present, require exact string equality with the configured PUBLIC_ORIGIN. Reject with 403 otherwise. fetch() always sends Origin on POST, so this is reliable on any modern browser.
(c) Content-Type: exact 'application/json' essence, for every request with a body.
(d) Double-submit CSRF token as the primary, browser-independent control: on any GET that establishes a session, set a second cookie bf_csrf = 32 random bytes hex, HttpOnly=false, SameSite=Lax, Secure, Path=/. Every mutation must echo it in an X-CSRF-Token header; compare with crypto.timingSafeEqual on equal-length buffers. Bind the CSRF value to the session (store it in the session record) so a token from a logged-out visitor cannot be replayed against someone else's session. This is ~25 lines, zero dependencies, and works even where Sec-Fetch-Site and SameSite do not.

WHY NOT SameSite=Strict: it would be stronger, but the product will be shared via links ('meet me here') opened from WhatsApp/Instagram, and Strict makes the user look logged out on that first navigation, which pushes people to re-enter credentials — a worse outcome. Lax plus (b) plus (d) is the right posture. If the owner later wants Strict, use the two-cookie pattern: a Strict primary and a Lax read-only cookie used purely to render 'you are signed in' on first paint.

ALSO: reject requests where Content-Length exceeds MAX_BODY_BYTES before reading the stream (currently the stream is drained up to the cap, which is fine, but an early reject on the declared length is cheaper), and lower MAX_BODY_BYTES for auth and location endpoints to 2KB — no legitimate request there is larger, and it caps the amount of attacker data hitting JSON.parse.

components.name: Account identity: verification, enumeration resistance, and invite-code discovery
components.purpose: Close both enumeration oracles and, more importantly, stop a stranger from receiving the location a user intended for a real friend.
components.design:
THE UNDERLYING BUG IS NOT THE ERROR MESSAGE — IT IS THAT EMAIL IS BOTH THE DISCOVERY KEY AND UNVERIFIED. Today anyone can register any address. If I register alice@example.com before Alice does, then when Bob adds 'alice@example.com' as a friend and turns on sharing, Bob sends his live position to me. Fixing the 404 string without fixing verification leaves the far worse hole open.

PRIMARY RECOMMENDATION — MAKE INVITE CODES THE DISCOVERY MECHANISM, NOT EMAIL. Give every user a rotatable invite code (8 chars, Crockford base32 from crypto.randomBytes, excluding vowels to avoid accidental words) and a link https://buisnessfind.app/add/<code>. Adding a friend means pasting a code or opening a link the other person deliberately sent you over a channel they already trust. This eliminates the enumeration oracle completely (there is nothing to enumerate — an 8-char base32 space is 10^12 and rate-limited), eliminates the impostor-registration attack (the code comes from the real person, not from an address anyone can claim), matches how Signal/WhatsApp-style invites actually work, and requires no email infrastructure at all. Add POST /api/friends/invite/rotate so a leaked code is disposable, cap a code at 25 uses, and expire codes after 30 days.

IF THE OWNER INSISTS ON EMAIL LOOKUP (keep it as a secondary path), then all three of these are mandatory together: (1) POST /api/friends/request always returns 202 {ok:true} with the copy 'If that address belongs to a buisnessfind account, they'll see your request.' — never 404, never a different status, never a different latency. When the address does not exist, store nothing (or store a pending invite keyed on sha256(email) that materialises at signup, but the sender's UI must show 'Invited' identically in both cases, or you have simply moved the oracle). (2) Only VERIFIED emails are lookup-able, and only the requester's own verified account may search. (3) Hard caps: 10 friend requests per hour and 20 per day per account, counted on attempts not successes, plus 5 lookups per minute. Without (3), 60/min is an 86,000-probe-per-day membership oracle for the entire user base.

EMAIL VERIFICATION IS REQUIRED. Zero npm dependencies does not mean zero email — call a transactional email REST API (Resend, Postmark, SES) with the built-in global fetch. That is a plain HTTPS POST and adds no packages. Flow: signup creates the account in state emailVerified:false and returns 202 with a GENERIC message ('Check your inbox to finish setting up your account') whether or not the email already exists — which closes the signup 409 oracle. If the address already belongs to an account, send that owner a 'someone tried to sign up with your address' email instead of a verification link. Unverified accounts can browse and search but CANNOT: be added as a friend, add friends, or enable any location share. Purge unverified accounts after 7 days. Add POST /api/auth/verify/resend, throttled to 3/hour.

IF THE OWNER TRULY WILL NOT SEND EMAIL, then invite codes become the only discovery mechanism (drop email lookup entirely), password reset is impossible and must be stated plainly at signup, and the enumeration question disappears with it. That is a coherent, honest design — email lookup without verification is not.

DISPLAY NAMES ARE ATTACKER-CONTROLLED. createUser does String(name).trim() with min length 1 and no maximum. Cap at 40 characters, NFKC-normalise, strip C0/C1 control characters and the Unicode bidi overrides (U+202A-U+202E, U+2066-U+2069) and zero-width characters, collapse whitespace, and reject strings containing '://' or a leading '@'. Otherwise an incoming friend request renders as 'buisnessfind Security ✓' or an RTL-spoofed name. The UI must never present a display name as verified identity — show the invite code fingerprint or the truncated email alongside it in the accept dialog.

STOP LEAKING EMAILS. publicUser() returns { id, name, email, createdAt } and is used by listIncomingRequests, so the email of anyone who sends you a request is disclosed — a harvesting primitive, and it discloses the requester to the recipient before any relationship exists. Split into publicUser (id, name, createdAt only) for all third-party contexts and selfUser (adds email) for /api/auth/me. Friends do not need each other's email either; if the accept dialog needs a disambiguator, show a masked form (a***e@example.com).

components.name: Friends graph: requests, cooldowns and caps
components.purpose: Make mutual-accept actually terminal — a 'no' must mean no — and bound harassment volume.
components.design:
HOLE 1 — INFINITE RE-REQUEST AFTER DECLINE. pendingRequestBetween() filters on status === 'pending' only, so respondToRequest sets 'declined' and the very next call to sendFriendRequest succeeds. An unwanted person can re-request every second, forever, at 60/min. FIX: in sendFriendRequest, look up the most recent request in EITHER direction regardless of status. If it is pending, 409. If it was declined within DECLINE_COOLDOWN_DAYS (30), refuse — but refuse with the same generic 202 the recipient-blocked case returns, so declining is not disclosed to the sender. Track declineCount on the (fromId,toId) pair; on the second decline, create an automatic silent block. Two 'no's is enough.

HOLE 2 — NO OUTBOUND CAP. One account can hold unlimited pending requests. Cap pending outbound at 50, total requests at 10/hour and 20/day, and friendships at 500. Count attempts, not successes, so failed probes consume budget.

HOLE 3 — DECLINE IS INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM NOTHING. Give the recipient a single control with three outcomes: Accept / Decline / Decline and block. Decline-and-block must be the same number of taps as decline; if blocking is buried, people do not use it.

HOLE 4 — REQUESTS ARE THE HARASSMENT CHANNEL. There is no message field today; do not add one. If the owner wants a note, cap it at 100 characters, render as text only (never innerHTML), and apply the same control/bidi stripping as display names.

DATA MODEL CHANGES. friendRequests: { id, fromId, toId, status: 'pending'|'accepted'|'declined'|'cancelled'|'expired', createdAt, respondedAt, declineCount, source: 'code'|'email' }. Enforce at most one non-terminal row per unordered pair. Expire pending requests after 30 days (status 'expired', purged at 90). Add POST /api/friends/cancel so a sender can withdraw — currently impossible.

friendships: canonicalise as userA < userB at insert time. Today friendshipKey() sorts at every comparison and areFriends() does an O(F) scan with a sort and a join per element; with listFriends() calling findById() (an O(U) array scan) per friend, friendLocations() is O(F * U) plus a full JSON re-serialisation on every write. Build a Map index of users by id at load, index friendships by userId into a Map<string, Set<string>>, and rebuild both on mutation. This is not cosmetic — /api/friends/locations is the hottest polled endpoint in the app.

removeFriend() is correct in that it deletes both share keys, but it must also: delete the in-memory location entry for each side if that was their last audience member, delete any pending requests between the pair, and write an entry to both users' activity logs so an unexpected unfriend is visible.

listFriends must return, per friend: { id, name, friendsSince, theyShareWithMe: bool, iShareWithThem: { active, expiresAt, precision } }. The UI needs both directions visible side by side; asymmetric sharing that the user cannot see at a glance is how people end up broadcasting to someone who gives nothing back.

components.name: Blocking and reporting
components.purpose: Add the two safety primitives that are entirely absent from the model, and make blocking undetectable to the blocked party.
components.design:
BLOCKS TABLE: { id, blockerId, blockedId, createdAt, reason: 'harassment'|'impersonation'|'spam'|'unwanted_contact'|'other'|null }. Stored one-directional (who blocked whom, for auditing and for un-blocking) but enforced bidirectionally.

ENFORCEMENT — a single isBlockedPair(a,b) helper checked at the TOP of every one of these paths, not sprinkled: sendFriendRequest (both directions), respondToRequest, setShare, updateLocation fan-out, friendLocations, listFriends, listIncomingRequests, checkin visibility, and any future presence feature. The default must be deny; a new endpoint that forgets the check is the failure mode, so route every friend-graph read through one authoritative canSee(viewerId, subjectId) function that returns false if either blocked the other, they are not friends, or the subject's account is disabled.

SIDE EFFECTS OF BLOCK, all atomic in one write: delete the friendship; delete BOTH share keys; purge the blocked party's cached view (server-side, so simply cutting the share suffices); delete all pending requests in both directions; remove each from the other's lists. Blocking must instantly stop an in-progress live location share — this is the emergency stop, so it must be one tap from the map view, not three levels into settings.

UNDETECTABILITY. A blocked user's friend request must return the identical 202 body, status and latency as a successful one. Their view of the ex-friend simply shows nobody sharing. Never return 403 'You are blocked' — that tells a stalker to make a new account, and it tells them which of several accounts belongs to their target. GET /api/friends/blocked is visible only to the blocker. Blocking is silent to the blocked party.

UNBLOCK: POST /api/friends/unblock { userId }, with a 24-hour cooling-off before the pair can become friends again, and NEVER an automatic restoration of the previous friendship or share — re-friending starts from zero. This matters: an abuser who talks their way into an unblock should not have location sharing silently resume at yesterday's settings.

REPORTS TABLE: { id, reporterId, subjectId, category: 'harassment'|'impersonation'|'spam'|'stalking'|'underage'|'other', note (<=1000 chars, text-only, sanitised), context: { requestId?, checkinId? }, createdAt, status: 'open'|'reviewed'|'actioned'|'dismissed', reviewedAt, reviewerNote }. POST /api/report, rate-limited to 10/day per reporter, available from the friend row, the incoming-request row and the profile sheet. Reporting must NOT require being friends — you can be harassed by a pending request.

OPERATIONAL SIDE. With no third-party services, the review queue is a file plus one admin-only endpoint. Specify: reports also fire a notification to the operator (email via fetch, or at minimum a line in an append-only reports.log so nothing is lost if store.json is rewritten). Add an isAdmin flag on the seed user and GET /api/admin/reports + POST /api/admin/reports/:id { status, action }. Admin actions needed: disable account (status 'disabled' — sessions killed, shares purged, location purged, cannot log in), and shadow-limit (can log in, cannot send friend requests). A location app WILL receive a stalking report; there must be a button to press on the day it arrives.

AUTO-BLOCK TRIGGERS, no human needed: second decline from the same sender; three distinct users blocking the same account within 30 days flags it for review and suspends its ability to send new requests; a report of category 'stalking' immediately and automatically stops all location shares FROM the reporter TO the subject.

SAFETY-CRITICAL DELETION EXCEPTION: when an account is deleted, reports AUTHORED by that user are retained in pseudonymised form (reporterId replaced with a salted hash), because the pattern of reports about an abuser must survive the victim closing their account. Disclose this in the privacy policy.

components.name: Location privacy engine
components.purpose: The core of the review. Replace 'we round the coordinates' with a real consent, expiry, visibility and minimisation system, on the assumption that the adversary is an accepted friend.
components.design:
PRINCIPLE: THE THREAT IS THE FRIEND. Every control below assumes the observer has already been accepted — because the realistic abuse is a partner, ex-partner, or someone who social-engineered one tap. Fuzzing defends against nobody in that model.

1. FUZZING AT 2dp IS NOT SUFFICIENT AND SHOULD BE DEMOTED FROM 'THE PROTECTION' TO 'ONE DISPLAY SETTING'. Math: 0.01 degrees latitude = 1.11km; longitude 1.11 * cos(lat), so ~0.98km at 28.6N. Cell area ~1.1 km2. Three failures. (a) DETERMINISTIC GRID SNAP IS STABLE — the same true position always maps to the same output, so an observer polling every 30 seconds accumulates a cell time series. The cell occupied 23:00-07:00 every night is the home cell; the 09:00-18:00 cell is work. The (home, work) pair is close to unique per individual even at kilometre granularity. (b) BOUNDARY FLAPPING — a user sitting still near a cell edge has GPS jitter that flips the reported cell back and forth, which tells the observer the true position lies on that boundary line: a sub-100m inference extracted from a nominally 1.1km fuzz. (c) CONDITIONAL PRIOR — a friend who already knows 'she lives in Lajpat Nagar' collapses 27,000 candidates to a building. Note the design cannot be fixed by switching to random jitter either: per-sample random offsets average away over N observations, which is strictly worse. If a coordinate transform is kept, it must be a PER-VIEWER, PER-EPOCH DETERMINISTIC offset — offset = f(HMAC(userSecret, viewerId || floor(now / 6h))) mapped into +/-400m, applied before the grid snap. That prevents two colluding friends from intersecting their views and prevents averaging, while remaining stable enough not to jitter on the map. But treat it as defence in depth, never as the reason the system is safe.

2. PRECISION IS A USER CHOICE, PER SHARE. Three levels, chosen at the moment of sharing, default not-exact: EXACT (as reported by GPS — for 'I'm outside the cafe, come find me'), AREA (~1km grid, the current behaviour, default), CITY (~10km, 1dp — 'I'm in Delhi'). Stored on the share record, applied at read time in friendLocations, so lowering precision takes effect for the next poll with no data migration. Store the highest-precision point once in memory and degrade per viewer on the way out.

3. MANDATORY EXPIRY — THE SINGLE MOST IMPORTANT FIX. Today db.locations[userId] is written by /api/location and never expires or is deleted; db.shares[key] = true is permanent. Share once, forget, and your 3am position is visible to that person for the life of the app. Specify: (a) EVERY SHARE HAS A REQUIRED expiresAt. The UI offers 15 minutes / 1 hour / 8 hours / 'until I leave this place'. There is deliberately NO 'until I turn it off' option — indefinite sharing is how passive forgetting becomes a tracker. Maximum 8 hours; extending requires a fresh tap. (b) THE POINT ITSELF EXPIRES INDEPENDENTLY: a stored coordinate older than 60 minutes is dead. friendLocations must FILTER on expiry, not merely return updatedAt and let the client decide — returning a stale point with an honest timestamp is still disclosing the position. (c) Purge the point on: logout, logout-all, last share expiring or being revoked, unfriend, block, password change, account deletion, and server restart.

4. LIVE COORDINATES SHOULD NEVER TOUCH DISK. Move `locations` out of the JSON store into an in-memory Map. Justification: they expire within an hour, so losing them on restart is CORRECT behaviour, not data loss; it keeps precise positions out of backups, out of any accidental commit, and out of anything an attacker who reads the filesystem or a subpoena can reach. It also removes a full-database JSON re-serialisation from the hottest write path. This single change lets the privacy policy say, truthfully, 'we never write your location to disk and we keep no location history'.

5. NO HISTORY, EVER — MAKE IT AN INVARIANT. The current design stores exactly one overwritten point per user. That is the right choice and must be documented as a deliberate invariant with a comment in the code, because 'add a breadcrumb trail' is the obvious next feature request and it changes the product's risk class entirely. (A client can of course build history by polling; that is unavoidable, which is precisely why duration limits and access logs matter more than fuzzing.)

6. WRITE-GATING: /api/location MUST REFUSE WHEN NOBODY IS SHARING. Today any logged-in client can POST coordinates whenever it likes, so a frontend bug or a future 'improvement' silently turns the search feature into a tracker. Enforce server-side: if the user has zero active, unexpired shares, return 409 {error:'No active shares'} and store nothing. This makes 'we only collect your location while you are actively sharing it' an enforced invariant rather than a client-side promise. Also range-check lat/lng (Number.isFinite is checked but the range is not), clamp accuracy, and reject updates more frequent than one per 20 seconds per user.

7. SEPARATE THE TWO CONSENTS. The browser geolocation prompt is consent to SEARCH NEARBY, not consent to be seen. Search coordinates must stay in the browser and go only to /api/nearby as a transient query. Sharing is a second, explicit, per-friend, time-boxed decision. The toggle copy must state exactly what happens, in the second person, at the moment of the tap: 'Rohan will see the area you're in (about a 1 km circle), updated while buisnessfind is open, until 6:40 PM. You can stop any time.' Never a bare toggle labelled 'Share location'. Require password re-entry to enable a share for the first time on a device, so someone holding a borrowed unlocked phone cannot silently switch it on.

8. VISIBILITY: 'WHO CAN SEE ME RIGHT NOW' IS MANDATORY. New GET /api/location/audience returning [{ friendId, name, precision, expiresAt, sharingStartedAt, lastViewedAt, viewCount }]. Surface it as a PERSISTENT, NON-DISMISSIBLE banner on the main map whenever any share is active: '2 people can see your location - Stop'. One tap to POST /api/location/stop-all. This is the highest-value single addition in the whole review: it converts 'trust the app' into 'check for yourself', and it is what makes a covertly-installed tracker fail, because the victim sees the banner.

9. ACCESS LOG. Record every read of your position: { viewerId, at } appended to a per-owner ring buffer (last 200 entries, 30-day retention, in memory plus periodic flush). Exposed at GET /api/location/access-log as 'Rohan checked your location 14 times today'. Frequency of observation is the signal that distinguishes a friend meeting you for coffee from someone monitoring you, and only the access log reveals it.

10. NOTIFY THE PERSON BEING WATCHED. In-app (and by email if wired): when a new share is enabled on their account, whenever a share is extended, and a weekly digest for any share that has been active more than 7 days ('You've been sharing your location with Rohan for 7 days - keep or stop?'). Notifications are how coerced or forgotten sharing surfaces. Rate-limit the digest so it cannot itself become a nuisance.

11. RECOMMENDED PRODUCT CHANGE — CHECK-INS AS THE DEFAULT, LIVE LOCATION AS THE EXCEPTION. The owner's copy is 'see where your friends are headed', which is fully satisfied by deliberate, per-event check-ins: 'Rohan is at Blue Tokai, Ansal Plaza - 20 minutes ago'. A check-in is a discrete act of publication tied to a business the app already knows, with an expiry (default 4 hours), no background collection, no polling, no continuous stream, and no home-cell inference — because people check in at cafes, not at their bedrooms. It is also cheaper (no /api/friends/locations polling) and more social. Make check-ins the headline feature; keep continuous live location as a deliberate, time-boxed, per-friend opt-in for the 'I'm on my way, watch me arrive' case. If the owner accepts only one recommendation from this entire review, it should be this one.

12. GHOST MODE / PANIC STOP. A single control that stops all sharing instantly, purges the stored point, and holds sharing off until explicitly re-enabled (sharingPausedUntil on the user record). Reachable from the map header, not from settings. This is the control someone reaches for in the moment they need it most.

13. KEEP COORDINATES OUT OF LOGS AND URLs. /api/nearby?lat=&lng= and /api/geocode?q= put precise user positions and searched addresses into every access log, proxy log and error trace — including the 502 path, which currently interpolates upstream response bodies into error messages. Convert both to POST with a JSON body, round the search coordinate to 3dp (~110m, ample for a nearby search) before it leaves the browser, and scrub coordinates from all server logs. Set Referrer-Policy: no-referrer so no page URL containing a location ever leaks to Google's tile hosts.

14. MINOR: round the updatedAt returned by friendLocations to the nearest minute. Millisecond timestamps reveal movement and app-foreground activity even when the reported cell is unchanged.

components.name: Rate limiting, abuse control and API cost protection
components.purpose: Close the unauthenticated-DoS and billing-drain paths, and stop the friend/location endpoints from being free abuse surface.
components.design:
THE COST-DRAIN BUG IS SERIOUS AND IMMEDIATE. /api/place and /api/nearby require no session. The only guard is 30 requests/min per IP and a global PLACE_DETAILS_DAILY_CAP of 200. One anonymous visitor at the limit exhausts the entire day's Place Details budget in about seven minutes — every day, for free, from a laptop — denying reviews to every real user while charging the owner for it (Place Details with reviews is the ~$40/1000 SKU, so a single day's cap is real money and a small script can guarantee it is spent by attackers rather than customers). FIXES, all needed: (1) require a verified session for /api/place; (2) add a per-user and per-IP daily sub-cap (e.g. 30 details/day/user) so no single actor can consume the global ceiling; (3) SERVER-SIDE CACHE place details by placeId with a 24-hour TTL — this is the big one, because it collapses cost for popular places, absorbs repeat lookups, and is comfortably inside Google's caching terms (Places content up to 30 days, place IDs indefinitely); (4) cache Nearby results keyed on (rounded lat/lng, category, radius) for 6 hours, which also means the rounding recommended above improves the hit rate; (5) reserve a slice of each cap for signed-in users so an anonymous flood cannot starve real ones; (6) add a monthly cap in addition to the daily one, and log a warning at 50/80/100 percent.

RATE LIMIT COVERAGE IS INCOMPLETE. Today the dispatcher rate-limits /api/friends (60/min) and the three places endpoints (30/min). NOT limited at all: all of /api/auth/* (so unauthenticated signup floods are unbounded, and each signup runs an ~80ms scrypt on the main thread — a CPU denial of service that needs no account and no cleverness), /api/location (which triggers a full-database JSON serialise and disk write per call), and /api/saved (which grows the database with attacker-controlled strings). Apply a single limiter to every route with a per-route budget:
  signup 5/hour/IP; login 20/15min/IP plus the per-email counter; verify-resend 3/hour; password-forgot 5/hour/IP and 3/day/email; friend-request 10/hour and 20/day per account; friends read 30/min; location write 1/20s per user; location read 20/min per user; saved write 60/hour, 500 rows/user hard cap; report 10/day; place 30/day/user; nearby 120/day/user.
  Key on userId when authenticated and on IP otherwise (IP alone is useless against IPv6 rotation). Use a bounded LRU rather than a plain Map — ipHits has a sweeper but loginAttempts does not, and neither is size-capped, so both are memory-exhaustion targets today.

BEHIND A PROXY, remoteAddress is the proxy for everyone, which collapses all users into one bucket and makes the 60/min friends limit a self-inflicted outage. Add TRUST_PROXY=1 gating X-Forwarded-For, and never read that header otherwise.

INPUT VALIDATION ON WRITES. savePlace stores body.placeId/name/category with no validation — undefined placeId is accepted, and up to ~8KB of arbitrary text is persisted per field. That is unbounded storage growth AND a stored-XSS payload if the frontend renders a saved-place name with innerHTML. Validate: placeId matches /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,255}$/, name <= 120 chars sanitised, category must be one of the 12 known keys, cap 500 saved rows per user, and never render any stored string with innerHTML (textContent only) regardless.

DURABILITY BUG. save() does fsp.writeFile directly onto store.json. A crash or a full disk mid-write truncates the entire user database — every account, gone. Write to store.json.tmp in the same directory, fsync, then fsp.rename (atomic on POSIX). Coalesce writes: mark dirty and flush at most every 250ms, plus a synchronous flush on SIGINT/SIGTERM/beforeExit. Keep the last 3 rotated copies. Also fix load(), which does a shallow spread merge, so a partially-corrupt file silently yields a half-empty database rather than refusing to start — validate the top-level shape and refuse to boot on mismatch rather than starting with an empty users array and re-seeding an admin account over live data.

SMALLER SERVER BUGS FOUND. handleSeoPage does an unguarded `seoPages[slug]` lookup, so /constructor and /toString reach prototype properties (routes is correctly guarded with hasOwnProperty; seoPages is not — make it consistent, and build both objects with Object.create(null)). serveStatic checks filePath.startsWith(PUBLIC_DIR) without a trailing separator, which would admit a sibling directory named public-anything — append path.sep. The 502 error path interpolates 300 characters of Google's response body into a message returned to the client, which can echo request details and key-related diagnostics — log it server-side, return a generic message. There is no Cache-Control: no-store on API responses, so /api/friends/locations is cacheable by an intermediary. There is no request timeout on the outbound fetch calls, so a slow Google response holds a socket indefinitely — add an AbortSignal.timeout(8000). And server.listen has no error handler for EADDRINUSE.

components.name: Legal surface: privacy policy, terms, export and deletion
components.purpose: Specify the disclosures a location-sharing app must make, and the user-facing data rights it must actually implement.
components.design:
PRIVACY POLICY — MUST COVER, SPECIFICALLY (a generic template is not adequate for a location product):
- WHAT IS COLLECTED: account (name, email, password hash), device/session metadata (hashed UA and IP prefix, and say so), search coordinates (transient, sent to Google, not stored), shared location (only while a share is active, in memory only, never written to disk, deleted within 60 minutes), saved places, check-ins, friend graph, location access log, reports.
- THE SENTENCE THAT MATTERS MOST, stated plainly and near the top: 'We do not keep a history of where you have been. We store at most one recent position, only while you are actively sharing it with someone you chose, and we delete it within an hour.' The architecture above makes this literally true, which is the point of building it that way.
- WHO CAN SEE YOUR LOCATION: only friends you individually and explicitly enabled, only for the duration you chose, at the precision you chose. Not other users. Not advertisers. State that the app operator can technically access data on the server, and under what circumstances they would (abuse investigation following a report).
- ACCURACY DISCLOSURE, honestly: 'Area' sharing shows an approximate ~1 km circle, and this reduces precision but does NOT make you anonymous to someone who already knows you — a friend who watches over time can infer where you live. Do not claim fuzzing makes sharing safe. Tell people to share only with people they actually trust. Underclaiming here is both ethically right and legally protective.
- THIRD PARTIES: Google Maps Platform receives search coordinates and place queries; link Google's Privacy Policy and Terms (this is a contractual requirement of the Maps/Places terms, alongside Google attribution on the map and on reviews). Name the email provider if one is used. State that no data is sold or used for advertising.
- RETENTION: sessions 90 days max; shared location <= 60 minutes; access logs 30 days; check-ins 4 hours visible then deleted; unverified accounts 7 days; declined requests 90 days; reports retained (pseudonymised) after the reporter deletes their account, with the safety reason given.
- LEGAL BASIS AND CONSENT (GDPR if any EU users): consent for location sharing, contract for account operation. Consent must be withdrawable as easily as given — which is what the audience banner and stop-all button provide. A location-sharing feature is high-risk processing; a short written DPIA is warranted even for a hobby project, and it is genuinely useful as a design document.
- INDIA / DPDP ACT 2023, since the owner is India-based: consent notice in plain language, itemised purpose, a named Data Protection Officer or grievance contact with a response commitment, and the right to correction and erasure. CRITICAL: the DPDP Act defines a child as anyone under 18 and prohibits tracking and behavioural monitoring of children outright. A location-sharing app therefore needs a hard 18+ gate at signup (date of birth, not a checkbox), not the usual 13+ line. Get this wrong and the feature is not merely risky, it is unlawful.
- CHANGES: material changes to location handling require notice and, for anything that broadens who can see a user, fresh consent — not a silent policy update.

TERMS OF USE — MUST INCLUDE: prohibited use clause naming stalking, monitoring another person without their knowledge, installing the app on someone else's device to track them, and creating an account in another person's name (impersonation) — with immediate termination as the stated consequence; 18+ requirement; user-generated content rules for display names, check-in notes and reports; that ratings and reviews are Google's content, shown under Google's terms, not the operator's and not editable; no warranty on business data accuracy or opening hours; that shared locations are self-reported by the device and can be inaccurate or deliberately falsified, so users must not rely on them for safety-critical purposes; limitation of liability; the reporting and enforcement process, including that accounts may be suspended pending review; and governing law/jurisdiction.

IN-PRODUCT SURFACE, not just linked pages: a plain-language summary at the first sharing prompt (not a wall of text at signup, which nobody reads); a 'Your data' settings screen listing what is held about you right now with a delete control beside each item; and the audience banner, which is the real-time embodiment of the consent promise.

EXPORT — GET /api/account/export returns a single JSON file: profile, friends (display names and dates only, never their emails — their data is not the requester's to export), saved places, check-in history, current share settings, access log, and reports authored. Note explicitly in the file and the UI that location history is absent because none exists. Rate-limit to 3/day.

DELETION — POST /api/account/delete requires the current password (re-authentication, so a borrowed phone cannot delete an account, and equally so a coerced user has a deliberate act). Behaviour must be: IMMEDIATELY and synchronously stop all shares, purge the in-memory location, kill all sessions, and remove the user from every friend's list; then soft-delete for 7 days (account unusable, cannot be logged into, email released for re-registration only after purge); then hard-purge users, sessions, friendships, requests, shares, saved places, check-ins and access logs. Retain only pseudonymised reports authored by the user, for the safety reason disclosed in the policy. The instant stop matters more than the eventual purge: someone deleting their account in a hurry is usually trying to stop being seen right now.

components.name: Final data model and endpoint list
components.purpose: The complete target state, so the implementing specialist has an unambiguous contract.

risks: CRITICAL - IMPOSTOR ACCOUNTS RECEIVE REAL PEOPLE'S LOCATIONS. There is no email verification, and friend discovery is by email. Register victim@gmail.com before the victim does, and when their friend adds that address and enables sharing, the attacker receives the live position. This is the single worst hole and it is not fixed by changing the 404 message. Fix: invite codes as the discovery mechanism, and/or mandatory email verification before an account can be a friend target or enable sharing.

CRITICAL - SHARED LOCATION NEVER EXPIRES. db.shares[key]=true and db.locations[userId] are both permanent. A user who shares once and forgets is broadcasting their position, including their home at 3am, indefinitely, with no expiry, no reminder, and no screen anywhere in the app that tells them who can see them. Fix: mandatory per-share expiresAt (max 8h, no 'indefinite' option), 60-minute point TTL enforced in friendLocations, and a persistent 'N people can see you - Stop' banner.

CRITICAL - 2dp FUZZING DOES NOT PREVENT HOME IDENTIFICATION. The grid snap is deterministic and stable, so repeated observation yields a cell time series whose nightly cell is the home cell, and GPS jitter across a cell boundary localises the user to that boundary at far better than 1 km. The observer is an accepted friend who already knows the neighbourhood, so a ~1.1 km2 cell is frequently decisive. Fuzzing must be demoted to a display preference; the real controls are expiry, audience visibility, an access log and check-ins instead of continuous tracking.

HIGH - TWO WORKING ACCOUNT ENUMERATION ORACLES PLUS A TIMING ORACLE. Signup returns 409 'An account with that email already exists'; POST /api/friends/request returns 404 'No account with that email' at 60 probes/minute (~86k/day) from a free unverified account; and login runs scryptSync only when the email exists, so response latency discloses membership even with a generic error string. All three need fixing together — generic 202s, hard per-account request caps, and a dummy scrypt verification on the not-found path.

HIGH - INFINITE RE-REQUEST AFTER DECLINE, AND NO BLOCKING AT ALL. pendingRequestBetween() only matches status 'pending', so a declined request can be re-sent immediately, forever, at 60/min. There is no blocks table, no report mechanism, and no admin action to take when a stalking report arrives. Fix: 30-day decline cooldown, auto-block on second decline, a blocks table enforced through one canSee() function, and a report queue with a disable-account action.

HIGH - THE APP CAN BE USED AS A COVERT TRACKER ON A BORROWED PHONE. Sharing can be enabled silently with one tap, never expires, sends no notification to the person being watched, and has no visible indicator. Fix: password re-auth to enable a share on a new device, mandatory expiry, a non-dismissible audience banner on the map, notifications to the watched user on enable/extend and weekly thereafter, and a one-tap stop-all.

HIGH - UNAUTHENTICATED BILLING DRAIN AND FEATURE DENIAL. /api/place needs no session; at the 30/min IP limit one laptop exhausts PLACE_DETAILS_DAILY_CAP=200 in about seven minutes, every day, spending the owner's money on the ~$40/1000 reviews SKU while denying reviews to every real user. Fix: session-gate it, add per-user daily sub-caps, and cache place details for 24 hours (which also cuts genuine cost substantially).

HIGH - scryptSync BLOCKS THE ONLY THREAD AND /api/auth/* IS EXEMPT FROM RATE LIMITING. Each signup or login stalls the entire server for ~80ms, and signup is completely unthrottled, so an unauthenticated flood is a straightforward CPU denial of service. Fix: async crypto.scrypt with a concurrency semaphore of 3 and a bounded queue, UV_THREADPOOL_SIZE=8, and a 5/hour/IP signup limit.

HIGH - NON-ATOMIC WRITE CAN DESTROY THE ENTIRE USER DATABASE. save() serialises the whole DB and calls fsp.writeFile directly onto store.json; a crash, a kill, or a full disk mid-write truncates every account. load() then shallow-merges the corrupt remains into an empty DB and the server happily re-seeds an admin account over the wreckage. Fix: write to a temp file, fsync, rename; keep rotated copies; refuse to boot on a shape mismatch instead of silently starting empty.

MEDIUM-HIGH - THE CSRF DEFENCE IS BYPASSABLE AND ABSENT WHERE IT MATTERS MOST. The content-type guard uses .includes('application/json'), which a CORS-safelisted 'text/plain; x=application/json' satisfies; it does not run on /api/auth/logout; and it does not exist at all on /api/friends, /api/location or /api/saved — so 'enable location sharing' is protected only by SameSite=Lax with nothing behind it. Fix: exact MIME essence match plus Origin/Sec-Fetch-Site plus a session-bound double-submit token, applied uniformly to every mutation.

MEDIUM-HIGH - COOKIE Secure IS OPT-IN. COOKIE_SECURE defaults off, so one forgotten env var on deploy ships session tokens over cleartext HTTP. Fix: default Secure on with an explicit dev opt-out, add the __Host- prefix, and send HSTS.

MEDIUM - ACCOUNT LOCKOUT AS A GRIEFING TOOL, AND AN UNPRUNED THROTTLE MAP. The IP+email key means anyone can lock a known email out for 15 minutes with 8 wrong guesses, on repeat; meanwhile loginAttempts is never swept or size-capped, so a stream of distinct emails is a memory-exhaustion vector. Fix: progressive delay instead of a hard lock, a separate global per-email counter, and a bounded LRU with a sweeper.

MEDIUM - UNVALIDATED, UNCAPPED USER STRINGS ARE PERSISTED AND RE-RENDERED. savePlace stores placeId/name/category with no validation or length limit (up to ~8KB each, unlimited rows), and display names have no maximum, no control-character stripping and no bidi-override stripping. This is unbounded storage growth, stored-XSS if the frontend ever uses innerHTML, and name-spoofing in the friend-request UI. Fix: strict validation, per-user row caps, NFKC + control/bidi stripping, and textContent-only rendering.

MEDIUM - EMAIL ADDRESSES LEAK THROUGH publicUser(). It returns the email, and listIncomingRequests uses it, so the address of anyone who sends you a request is disclosed before any relationship exists. Split into publicUser (no email) and selfUser (email).

MEDIUM - PRECISE COORDINATES TRAVEL IN GET QUERY STRINGS. /api/nearby?lat=&lng= and /api/geocode?q= write user positions and searched addresses into every access log, proxy log and error trace, and the 502 handler echoes 300 characters of upstream response body back to the client. Fix: POST with JSON bodies, round search coordinates to 3dp client-side, scrub logs, and return generic upstream errors.

MEDIUM - DPDP ACT AGE PROBLEM. India's DPDP Act 2023 defines a child as under 18 and prohibits tracking or behavioural monitoring of children outright, so a location-sharing app needs a hard 18+ gate with a date of birth, not the customary 13+ checkbox. Shipping without it is a legal exposure, not just a policy gap.

MEDIUM - NO PASSWORD RESET, NO EMAIL VERIFICATION, NO DEVICE LIST, NO ACCOUNT DELETION exist anywhere in the current code. For a location-sharing product, being unable to see and kill an unknown signed-in session, or to delete an account and stop being seen immediately, is a safety failure rather than a missing convenience.

MEDIUM - PERFORMANCE PATH THAT BECOMES A DoS. friendLocations -> listFriends -> findById is an O(friends x users) array scan on the hottest polled endpoint, and every /api/location write re-serialises the entire database to disk. Fix: Map indexes rebuilt on mutation, coalesced writes, and keeping locations in memory only — which is also the right privacy answer.

LOW-MEDIUM - SMALLER SERVER DEFECTS: unguarded seoPages[slug] lookup reaches prototype properties (routes is guarded, seoPages is not); serveStatic's startsWith check lacks a trailing separator; no Cache-Control: no-store on API responses; no timeout on outbound fetch to Google; verifyPassword feeds attacker-controllable N straight into scrypt without clamping; and remoteAddress-based limiting collapses every user into one bucket behind a reverse proxy.
